chains.title: Alt T allele creates a C/EBP site bound by CEBPA, raising hepatic SORT1 (and PSRC1/CELSR2) and lowering LDL/MI risk
chains.element: EH38E1374646 (dELS enhancer, chr1:109274794-109275142; Ensembl regulatory ENSR1_CDSQQ)
chains.cell_type: Hepatocyte (HepG2 ChIP evidence; Hep 3B2.1-7 expression context, DepMap ACH-000625)

links.claim: The alt T allele creates a strong bZIP C/EBP-type site in vitro: QBiC-SELEX group G035 (CEBPB/CEBPA/CEBPE own models) gives z 22.81, effect +2.331, site moving from the 87.0th to the 99.8th percentile of k-mer coefficients. Within this specificity group CEBPA is chosen because (i) ENCODE ChIP-seq shows a CEBPA peak containing the variant in HepG2 (ENCSR142IGM) while no CEBPB peak is found in HepG2, and (ii) CEBPA is by far the most expressed group member in the hepatic context (141.33 TPM vs CEBPB 4.05, CEBPE 0.0). ChIP shows occupancy, not yet allele-specificity.

The variant lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E1374646, DNase z 4.9, H3K27ac z 4.8, maxima across biosamples) also annotated as an enhancer regulatory feature by VEP; CEBPA occupancy in HepG2 shows the element is accessible and TF-bound in a liver line.

In liver, the alt T allele raises SORT1 expression (GTEx NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), with concordant increases of PSRC1 (+1.24) and CELSR2 (+1.04); Open Targets gives SORT1 the top L2G score (0.99) across lipid credible sets with PIP 1.00, so SORT1 is the leading target although the eQTL does not by itself separate the three co-regulated genes.
The hepatocyte is the relevant cell type: CEBPA binds the element in HepG2, is highly expressed in the hepatic line, and the eQTL signal is from liver tissue.

Higher hepatic SORT1 on the T allele alters VLDL/LDL handling and lowers LDL and total cholesterol; the common G allele is the high-cholesterol/risk allele in GWAS (p ~1e-323) and the locus colocalizes with myocardial infarction.

chains.title: CEBPB, not CEBPA, is the bZIP factor gained at the alt allele driving SORT1

links.claim: The best model of group G035 is CEBPB's own model (z 22.81, effect +2.331, alt binds more), and CEBPB ChIP peaks contain the variant in four non-hepatic biosamples (A549, HeLa-S3, IMR-90, MCF-7), showing the created site is a usable C/EBP site; however no CEBPB peak is found in HepG2 and CEBPB is only 4.05 TPM in the hepatic line, which weakens this chain.
The created site lies in the active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, occupied by C/EBP-family factors in several cell types.
The element's output is SORT1 (best L2G 0.99), though CELSR2 (0.98) and PSRC1 (0.66) are co-scored and all three are up on the alt allele in liver.
Hepatocytes under CEBPB-inducing conditions (acute-phase/inflammatory), where CEBPB protein can rise above its low basal transcript level.
Changed SORT1 dose shifts LDL cholesterol and myocardial infarction risk at 1p13.

chains.title: CEBPG is the gained bZIP factor at the alt allele

links.claim: CEBPG's own model gives the largest bZIP z in the screen (G143: z 26.76, effect +2.321, site 64.5th -> 99.4th percentile) and CEBPG is well expressed (46.37 TPM); z is a significance, not a strength, ranking, and no ChIP evidence for CEBPG at this site is available (the only hepatic C/EBP peak shown is CEBPA).
The created site is in the active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646.
SORT1 is the leading target of this element (L2G 0.99) and its liver expression rises with the alt allele (NES +1.27).
Hepatocyte context, where CEBPG is abundantly expressed (46.37 TPM) and the liver eQTL is observed.
Higher SORT1 lowers LDL cholesterol and MI risk at this locus.

predictions: CEBPG ChIP shows allele-specific binding at the variant while CEBPA ChIP signal is not allele-biased
CEBPG knockdown lowers SORT1 specifically in T-allele cells
CEBPG-ATF4 heterodimer motif mutations abolish the allelic difference

chains.title: An RFX-family factor (RFX5) gains binding at the alt allele and drives the element

links.claim: RFX-specificity models gain binding at the alt allele (G094: RFX7 z 18.73, RFX5 z 11.53, effect +0.788; G028 RFX4/RFX1 concordant). RFX5 is chosen on expression alone (41.14 TPM), the predicted effect is smaller than for the C/EBP groups, and there is no ChIP evidence for RFX at this site.
The site is in the active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646.
SORT1 is the leading candidate target, up on the alt allele in liver.
Hepatocytes, where RFX5 is well expressed (41.14 TPM) and the eQTL is observed.
SORT1 dosage change moves LDL cholesterol and MI risk.

predictions: RFX5 ChIP shows allele-specific occupancy at the variant
RFX5 knockdown, not C/EBP knockdown, flattens the allelic reporter difference
Mutating the X-box half-site, not the C/EBP core, removes the allelic effect
falsified_if: No RFX occupancy at this element in liver data
C/EBP core mutation abolishes the allelic difference while X-box mutation does not

grades_v0.reason: E12 is a QBiC-SELEX prediction alone (z 22.81, alt binds more). CEBPA is chosen on expression (E12 lists 141.33 TPM), which is a reasoned choice. No ChIP or allelic assay shows CEBPA binding here.

E03 and E01 place the variant in a dELS cCRE with high DNase and H3K27ac. The z-scores are maxima over biosamples, so liver or Hep3B activity is not shown. This is context only and gives no allelic effect.

E05 gives L2G SORT1 0.99 and a liver SORT1 sQTL (PIP 0.72), but CELSR2 (0.96) and PSRC1 are also scored. The sQTL is splicing, not expression. E06a names different lead variants (rs12740347, rs646776) and does not support an enhancer-to-SORT1 link for this SNP. No perturbation evidence is cited.
Hep3B expression of CEBPA is shown (E12) and the sQTL is from liver (E05). No chromatin or CEBPA occupancy data from hepatocytes is shown, and the cCRE biosample is unspecified.

E04 supports the LDL association, and E06b gives MI colocalization (PH4 0.855). The claimed direction conflicts with the data: E04 lists G as the effect allele for high cholesterol, but one LDL row lists T. The mechanistic link from SORT1 to LDL is not shown by E06c, which only lists SORT1 generally.
CEBPB has its own model with a strong z (E12), but it is the low-expressed member (4.05 TPM). The claim that it could be the occupying paralog is speculative, and there is no ChIP evidence.
Same cCRE context as H1 (E03, E01). It does not distinguish paralogs and shows no allelic effect.
L2G favours SORT1 (E05) but CELSR2 scores almost as high. The claim omits that; there is no perturbation evidence.
CEBPB expression of 4.05 TPM in Hep3B (E12) is low. Hepatocyte relevance is asserted, not shown by evidence.
E04 and E06b link the locus to LDL and MI, but not through CEBPB or the stated direction.

E09 and E16 are binding predictions only. Group G143 has a higher z than G035, but z is not a strength ranking. CEBPG is chosen on its own model and 46 TPM, with no assay. CEBPD (E16) is bundled in the title, but H3 names one TF.
E03 gives only generic cCRE context with no allelic information.
E05 is cited only generally. SORT1 is not named in the claim, and CELSR2 scores similarly.
E09 only shows expression in the Hep3B context (46.37 TPM). No evidence is cited that CEBPG works in hepatocytes.
E04 and E06c show only a general association with LDL and SORT1, nothing specific to CEBPG.

E15 and E11 are binding predictions only. RFX5 sits in a group whose best model is RFX7 and whose RFX5 z is 11.53. The choice rests on expression alone. Whether RFX5 recognises this motif is unclear, and the predicted effect is smaller than for the C/EBP groups.
E03 gives the generic active cCRE context.
E05 favours SORT1 but does not tie it to RFX. It is the same non-specific evidence as for the other chains.
E15 shows only RFX5 expression of 41 TPM, with no evidence that it is relevant in hepatocytes.
E04 gives the generic LDL association, nothing RFX-specific.

grades_final.reason: The QBiC-SELEX gain on the alt allele (G035, z 22.81, effect +2.331) is only a binding prediction. The choice of CEBPA is argued from a HepG2 peak (E19) and expression, which gives occupancy without allele-specificity. The claim itself concedes this. CEBPA's own model (z 22.63) is not shown as a separate row, so a qbic_tf_detail lookup is worth running.

The cCRE is a dELS with strong DNase and H3K27ac, and VEP annotates an enhancer. These z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not liver-specific. The HepG2 CEBPA peak shows occupancy near the variant, not enhancer activity or allelic function.

The liver eQTL (E20) is strong, with SORT1 NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54, and the Open Targets L2G for SORT1 is 0.99, which gives genetic and colocalisation support. However, PSRC1 and CELSR2 co-vary, and neither the eQTL nor L2G isolates the target. The claim acknowledges this. The link from the element to SORT1 is not shown by perturbation.
The liver eQTL and the HepG2 CEBPA peak are consistent with hepatocytes. CEBPA expression is quoted for Hep 3B2.1-7. There is no hepatocyte-specific perturbation or allele-specific data.

The GWAS (effect allele G, strongest for high cholesterol) and eQTL directions agree: T raises SORT1 and lowers LDL. E06b supports MI colocalisation of rs12740374. No evidence cited shows SORT1 dose mediates the phenotype, and the mechanistic link via CEBPA is not shown. The literature quote E06a names different lead variants, which weakens the single-variant claim.

CEBPB has its own model and the alt allele binds more (z 22.81). The ChIP peaks are in non-hepatic cells only, with none in HepG2, and expression is low (4.05 TPM). This is a prediction with indirect support. The claim itself concedes it is weak.
The cCRE epigenomic marks are real but are maxima over biosamples. CEBPB peaks in A549, HeLa-S3, IMR-90 and MCF-7 are not hepatic, so they do not show the element is bound in liver.
The eQTL and L2G support SORT1 at the locus level (E20, E05). The link to CEBPB at this element is not shown, and the gene is not separated from CELSR2 and PSRC1.

The claim relies on CEBPB induction under inflammatory conditions. No cited evidence shows induction or CEBPB activity in hepatocytes. E12 gives only 4.05 TPM, and E20 is a liver eQTL that says nothing about CEBPB.
The GWAS and E06b link the locus to LDL and MI. They do not implicate CEBPB or show SORT1 dose as mediator. The direction is not stated.
CEBPG has its own model and the alt allele binds more (z 26.76, 64.5th to 99.4th percentile). This is only an in vitro prediction. There is no ChIP support, and the claim admits this.
The cCRE is active (E03), but the evidence is general and unrelated to CEBPG occupancy.
The liver eQTL and L2G support SORT1 at the locus level. Nothing links CEBPG to the element, and CELSR2 and PSRC1 are not separated.
CEBPG expression (46.37 TPM) is cited from E09 and the liver eQTL is from E20. Neither shows CEBPG activity in hepatocytes, so the support is only expression context.
The GWAS and E06b link the locus to LDL and MI, consistent in direction. No evidence ties CEBPG or SORT1 dose to the phenotype.

The RFX groups predict alt gain (G094 effect +0.788, G028 concordant). RFX5 was chosen on expression alone, without ChIP or a TF-specific reason. The G094 best model is RFX7, and RFX5 (z 11.53) is a lower-ranked member. This is a prediction alone with a smaller effect.
The cCRE is active, but the evidence does not tie RFX to the element.
The liver eQTL and L2G support SORT1 at the locus level (E05, E20), but nothing links the element to SORT1 through RFX5, and CELSR2 and PSRC1 are not excluded.
RFX5 is expressed at 41.14 TPM and a liver eQTL exists. Neither shows RFX5 acting at this element in hepatocytes.
The GWAS links the locus to LDL and MI. The effect allele and direction are unstated, and nothing connects RFX5 or SORT1 dose to the phenotype.

The co-localization analysis, based on two-sample Mendelian randomization results, revealed that single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs12740374 (PH4 = 0.855) was causally associated with MI and a balanced diet(I eat all of the above), while SNP rs7528419 (PH4 = 0.716) was causally associated with CHD and a balanced diet.

GWASs and sequencing studies have identified key genetic variations associated with CAD, including JCAD/KIAA1462, GUCY1A3, PCSK9, and SORT1, which regulate inflammation, lipid metabolism, and vascular function.
